title: How Far Back the Payment Record Counts in an Auto Loans Due Day Realignment
content:
**The realigned day is settled only after the loan stands current with no installment past due on its records.** While the loan's records still show an installment whose due date has passed and which is not satisfied, the realigned day is not yet settled.

How far back the scheduled installments counted for the record credit reach, on a loan of the Auto Loans line, follows how long that loan has been on the books, counted in whole months from the date it funded to the day of the realignment.

1. Where the loan was funded less than 24 whole months before the realignment, the scheduled installments counted are those credited in the last twelve months.
2. Where the loan was funded at least 24 but less than 36 whole months before the realignment, the scheduled installments counted are those credited in the last twenty-four months.
3. Where the loan was funded at least 36 whole months before the realignment, the scheduled installments counted are all those credited over the life of the loan.

## The three windows compared on one loan

Take a loan that has taken 44 scheduled installments since funding, of which 11 fell in the last twelve months and 23 in the last twenty-four. Read under the first window it counts 11; under the second, 23; under the third, 44. Which window applies is settled by the loan's age alone.

## The months at which the window changes

A loan funded exactly 24 whole months before the realignment counts over the last twenty-four months. A loan funded exactly 36 whole months before counts over the whole life of the loan. A loan funded 23 whole months before counts over the last twelve months.
